text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ministries of finance and petroleum disagree over who should handle funds intended for Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation.
- Volume of exports from Tin Can Island port in Lagos was over 15 percent higher in first quarter of 1997 than in same period last year.
- Flour millers have sent protest letter to International Institute of Tropical Agriculture after some scientists there suggested Nigeria should be importing less wheat.
- French firm Total likely to acquire rights to Ashland oil production concessions.
- Environmental health experts have issued warning against eating fruit and vegetables grown in some parts of northern city of Kaduna because of chemical contamination from nearby textile industries.
- Ministry of Works and Housing wants money for road maintenance from Petroleum Trust Fund, set up to cushion impact of 1994 rise in fuel prices through spending on special projects.
- Northern Katsina state has introduced tax on livestock to help fund improvements to grazing land. Herders will have to pay 60 naira for a cow and 20 naira for a sheep.
